claims.text: The baseline HVAF-i7 deposition uses 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl powder.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition produces acceptable coating quality but insufficient coating thickness.
Increasing HVAF-i7 process-gas pressure increases particle velocity.
Increased particle velocity raises particle kinetic energy.
Elevated particle kinetic energy decreases splat rebound.
Elevated particle kinetic energy improves particle flattening during impact.
Reduced rebound and enhanced inter-splat bonding increase the efficiency of coating-layer buildup.
The additional particle energy produces more effective in-flight heating.
The pressure-induced changes in particle impact produce better deformation and reduced coating porosity.
Increasing process-gas pressure will produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat than the baseline process.
Increasing process-gas pressure will produce a denser and more homogeneous bond coat than the baseline process.
Increasing process-gas pressure will improve bond-coat adhesion.
The pressure-modified coating will be less prone to as-sprayed oxidation.
A carefully calibrated pressure increase will preserve oxidation resistance and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
A spray distance of approximately 350 mm is suitable for both flat substrates and internal geometries down to 120 mm in diameter.
Excessive particle velocity may damage the substrate or coating structure.

contradictions.description: Maintaining an approximately 350 mm spray distance while depositing inside a 120 mm internal diameter is geometrically inconsistent for a conventional radial standoff unless a specialized axial or angled arrangement is specified.
